items.title: What Hurricane Season Means For Hospitality’s Capex
items.summary: Host Hotels & Resorts’ $105 million work on The Don CeSar puts a real number on the cost of hurricane repairs and preparedness — but, as the company notes, investing in resilience doesn’t reduce risk to zero.

items.title: Google Strips Out EU Travel Search Features to Avoid More Fines
items.summary: Google is scaling back certain search features in Europe as DMA enforcement escalates.

items.title: Inside the Financial Engineering of Club Med’s IPO
items.summary: Club Med wants to grow from 69 resorts to about 85 without owning the next wave, and its new financial structure helps explain why.

items.title: Luxury+Lifestyle: Can a Small Collection of Iconic London Hotels Out-Earn Big Brands?
items.summary: The owner of The Connaught and The Berkeley has hired the man who scaled Six Senses to build an operating company for luxury lifestyle hotels it owns and doesn't own.

items.title: Skift Global Forum Preview: Intrepid’s Chairman on the Climate Cost His Rivals Sidestep
items.summary: You created the demand, so you own the emissions. That's Darrell Wade's case for counting the customer flights most operators leave off their carbon books, and the competitive cost it carries. We'll test whether the industry can afford to follow at Skift Global For

items.title: Everyone Is All In on the Airbus A321XLR — Except Delta
items.summary: More airlines are embracing long-haul flying on narrowbody jets — in a competitive transatlantic market, they allow airlines to launch service in smaller cities. However, Delta is not convinced.

items.title: How Wellness Hospitality Is Breaking Out of the Luxury Bubble
items.summary: Health-conscious travel is entering the mainstream. Novotel’s Longevity Everyday model shows how hotel brands can extend wellness beyond premium retreats by embedding supportive choices into the ordinary rhythms of a stay.

items.title: Flagship Group Makes First Three Acquisitions For Experiences Roll-Up
items.summary: Appetite for an experiences roll-up has long existed, but Covid put plans on ice. Now P&Ls have had a chance to rebound, and the timing is perhaps even better today, with experiences positioned as a counter-AI play.
